_meta.control_type: GROUP E — CEILING TEST. Does the defensibility scale's LEVEL 5 actually exist / is it reachable?
_meta.purpose: Sean: 'any company that has significant IP or flywheel will have high defensibility... These companies are a 5.' Every one of the 16 prior cases scored 1-4 and NO input ever mentioned a patent, trade secret, flywheel or switching cost. Level 5 was unreachable by construction. This case supplies a canonical level-5 business to test whether the top of the scale exists in practice.
_meta.prediction: Defensibility 5/5. A score of 4 or below means the top level is unreachable and the scale is effectively 1-4.
_meta.ground_truth: ASML holds a 100% monopoly on EUV lithography, >90% of the global lithography market, 2,000+ EUV patents, exclusive Zeiss optics supply (ASML owns ~24.9% of Zeiss SMT), a 5,000-supplier parts network, 30 years of R&D, and installed-base lock-in on which every leading-edge fab depends. Independent analysts describe it as 'compounding barriers that no competitor has shown the ability to overcome'.

form.category: Semiconductor lithography equipment — extreme ultraviolet (EUV) and deep ultraviolet (DUV) systems used to print circuitry onto silicon wafers for chip fabrication.
form.positioning_sentence: The only company in the world that can supply EUV lithography systems.
form.differentiator: We hold a complete monopoly on EUV lithography — there is no second supplier, and we control over 90% of the global lithography market. This rests on more than 2,000 EUV patents covering the technology, developed over 30 years of R&D at a cost no competitor could justify repeating. Our optics come from Zeiss exclusively, and we hold a stake in Zeiss SMT so that supply cannot be redirected to a rival; the light source, the optics and the precision mechanics are integrated such that no single component can be substituted. We are supported by a network of around 5,000 suppliers that took decades to assemble and is not replicable. Once a fab is built around our machines, the tooling, process recipes and process control are all calibrated to us, so the installed base cannot switch. Every leading-edge semiconductor in the world is produced on our equipment, and the leading-edge nodes cannot be manufactured without it.
form.undercut_on: Nothing that matters. Competitors have attempted EUV development and withdrawn — the engineering and capital requirements were prohibitive. We are not cheaper; we are the only option. The residual risk is geopolitical export controls and our customers' own capex cycles, neither of which is a competitor.
form.your_price_point: Not price-competitive by design — each EUV system costs well over US$100M and is priced on value and scarcity.
form.their_price_point: No competing EUV product exists at any price.

competitors_named: Canon (DUV and nanoimprint — no EUV capability)
Nikon (DUV only — withdrew from EUV development)
Applied Materials / Lam Research (adjacent deposition and etch, not lithography)
Chinese state-backed lithography efforts (SSMB and domestic EUV programmes)
customer_description: A very small number of leading-edge semiconductor manufacturers — TSMC, Samsung, Intel and, where permitted, SMIC. The trigger is building or expanding a leading-edge fabrication line, which is impossible without EUV.

derived_competitive_set.derivation_method: Derived from published patent assessments, supplier-chain analysis and the disclosed structure of the lithography market.

members: not manufacturing leading-edge chips at all
designing chips fabricated by someone else

tier_1_cheap_substitute.price_floor: DUV systems are far cheaper but cannot reach leading-edge geometries.
tier_1_cheap_substitute.why: A genuine lower-cost route, which caps the addressable market but does not touch the leading edge.

tier_2_direct_set.why: The only entities that compete in lithography at all — none with a shipping EUV product.

members: ASML — owns 'the only EUV supplier' outright, globally and completely
tier_3_category_incumbent.why: Unlike every other case in the ladder, there is no contest for the incumbent position. It is absolute.
tier_3_category_incumbent.diagnostic: The strongest possible Tier 3: a monopoly on the category's defining capability.

tier_4_adjacent_crossover.why: Occupy the same fab floor and the same capital budget, but do not print features.

chip design moving to architectures that need less leading-edge silicon

_expected_reasoning.market_headroom: Very large and growing, driven by AI compute demand. Expected 4-5.
_expected_reasoning.competitive_room: Zero effective competition in EUV. Expected 5.
_expected_reasoning.mental_advantage: The default and only answer for EUV. Expected 5.
_expected_reasoning.defensibility: **THE TEST.** 2,000+ patents, exclusive optics supply, non-substitutable integration, installed-base lock-in, 30 years of R&D, 5,000-supplier network. Expected **5**. Anything below 5 means level 5 is unreachable in practice.
_expected_reasoning.demand_reach: Extremely few buyers (~5), but total penetration within them and no alternative. Expected 3-4.

_what_this_case_uniquely_tests: Whether the top of the defensibility scale exists. It is also the project's first case where the business is unambiguously, globally dominant AND richly IP-protected — the exact combination Sean named as a 5.
